evidence.detail: apply_rules_to_decks: when len(archetypes) > 1 it unconditionally sets rule_archetype_name = 'Bad rules'. No parent-child resolution exists.
The SQL groups by deck_id and checks COUNT(DISTINCT archetype_id) >= 1; the HAVING clause makes no use of archetype_closure ancestry.
archetype_closure table with ancestor/descendant/depth columns exists and supports parent-child queries, but is not used in rule matching.
apply_rules_query: exclusion via rule_card.include=FALSE already exists (for specific cards), but there is no mechanism to express color-land exclusion rules.

triage.notes: Two distinct sub-features: (1) parent-child resolution — requires joining archetype_closure in apply_rules_to_decks to detect ancestry, then picking the deepest (most specific) archetype; (2) color-awareness for exclusion rules — would require knowing what colors each land produces, a separate and substantially more complex addition. Neither part is trivially isolated.
